subject: physics
question_text: Write the expression for Stokes' law.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 10 Mechanical Properties of Fluids, Very Short Answer Question 13 (printed p.106). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: Stokes' law gives the viscous drag on a small sphere moving slowly through a fluid as F = 6πηrv, with η the coefficient of viscosity, r the radius of the sphere and v its velocity; it holds only while the flow around the sphere stays streamline, which needs the sphere small and its speed low.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.margin_note: First mark. Write F = 6πηrv and name every symbol.
steps.why: Naming every symbol is what turns the formula into an answer — F, η, r and v each stand for a specific quantity in the same setup.
common_mistakes: Writing F = 6πrv or F = 6ηrv, missing one of the four factors.
Not naming the symbols — the formula alone, unlabelled, is an incomplete answer.

steps.margin_note: Second mark. Say it needs a small sphere moving slowly, so the flow stays streamline.
steps.why: Stokes' law is derived assuming streamline flow around the sphere. A large sphere or a high speed turns the flow turbulent, and the formula no longer applies.
common_mistakes: Giving the formula alone without the condition — a sphere moving fast enough to turn the flow turbulent is not covered by F = 6πηrv.
Saying the condition is a small fluid rather than a small, slow-moving sphere.

recall.must_convey: That Stokes' law holds only for a small sphere moving slowly, so that the flow around it stays streamline.
accept: not valid once flow turns turbulent
reject: F equals six pi eta r v

steps.memory_tip: Small and slow keeps the flow streamline — that is when Stokes' law holds.

insider_note: One mark for F = 6πηrv with every symbol named, one for the condition it needs: a small sphere moving slowly enough to keep the flow streamline.
